items.question: What is ABDM Sandbox?
items.answer: Sandbox is a space for experiment of integration before the digital health product is made live for the actual use. The integration for any health solution which intends to work in the ABDM ecosystem is first done in the sandbox in the environment. This is necessary to test the robustness, security function, etc. of the integrating ecosystem for various parameters before they are formally integrated into the ecosystem. Once these tests are done, the production key is provided in Sandbox environment and they can start their operations. This step has been introduced to ensure that the systems are first tested before they are made available to participants in the ABDM.

items.question: Who can participate in the ABDM Sandbox?
items.answer: Any entity or individual, including any HMIS, LMIS, PHR app, Health locker, Health tech company, Tech company etc. can potentially participate in ABDM signing in on our Sandbox.

items.question: How do I participate in ABDM Sandbox?
items.answer: Please apply at How do I participate? section

items.question: What are the different Milestones in ABDM Sandbox?
items.answer:
There are mainly three different Milestones: - 

➢ Milestones#1 - ABHA creation (optional) and capture & verification for seamless patient registration. Completion of this Milestone will enable any healthcare entity or a patient to generate ABHA with Aadhar/Mobile/PAN/Passport/Driving License. Currently, system is built to facilitate ABHA creation by Aadhar/Mobile/Driving Licence. This milestone will also enable to capture, verify and discover the already existing ABHA.

 ➢ Milestones#2 - Building Health Information Provider (HIP) services to share digital records via Personal Health Records (PHR) app. Completion of this milestone enables a health care entity/professional to become Health Information Provider (HIP). This implies that the clinical artifacts generated will be linked with the ABHA and is ready for consent-based-sharing within ABDM eco-system. Patient will be able to view the generated and linked health records in any of his/her preferred PHR app downloaded in the mobile device.

 ➢ Milestones#3 - Developing Health Information User (HIU) services to provide view of patient’s medical history to authorized healthcare workers with complete consent. Completion of this milestone enables a healthcare entity/professional to become Health Information User (HIU). This milestone enables exchange of health data between healthcare entities or healthcare professionals or with a health locker based on patient authentication only. Any entity seeking health records for treatment/diagnosis is termed as Health Information User (HIU)

items.question: What are the prerequisites for integration?
items.answer: Integrator need to create user credential for Sandbox (i.e, Client ID and secure) and then generate authorization token using this client ID and secure (from Postman). After that end - point URL need to be registered on dev services dev.abdm.gov.in/devservice/v1/bridges .

items.question: How can we obtain Authorization token?
items.answer: You may refer to Getting started with APIs

items.question: What should be the format for Authorization header?
items.answer: Authorization header must have format as Bearer (token \_ value) i.e, prefix Bearer followed by space before token value.

items.question: What are the differences between API Version#1 and Version#2?
items.answer:
ABDM has introduced integration APIs as Ver. 1 and Ver. 2. Enhanced security measures have been introduced in version 2 APIs:- 

➢ Sensitive data like otp, Aadhaar no., password, username etc have to be encrypted. 

➢ Data is encrypted by public certificate. The certificate can be downloaded from     /v2/auth/cert API under Authentication tag in the version 2.

 ➢ RSA encryption to encrypt the data.

items.question: What are the different methods for ABHA registration?
items.answer:
At present mainly 3 methods are used for ABHA registration: -

a) Registration via Aadhaar 

b) Registration via Mobile : to be deprecated 

c) Registration via other ID documents like (PAN, DL, Passport etc under progress)

➢ Registration via Aadhaar : an integrator needs to generate an Aadhaar OTP, followed by OTP verification. Once the OTP is verified, the client is returned complete profile data along with ABHA no.

➢ Registration via Mobile : an integrator needs to first generate OTP for the user provided mobile. After generating OTP, mobile OTP is verified and a transaction ID is returned to the client. Along with this transaction ID, demographic details of the user are captured and on the basis of this, ABHA no. is generated. 

➢ Registration via other documents : Currently we support Driver Licence for ABHA generation. The user is requested his/her mobile no. to be linked with ABHA no. An OTP is sent to the given mobile number and after verifying the OTP, demographic information of the user is captured along with DL number.

items.question: Do I require WASA for the full application?
items.answer: Yes, WASA required to be done for the full application if not done before and the Safe-to-Host certificate is not issued to the application.

items.question: Do I require WASA if I have Safe-to-host certificate for the application?
items.answer: No, WASA is not required if Safe-to-Host certificate is already issued for the application. However, if safe-to-host certificate has expired, then the same must be renewed as per the certificate validity.

items.question: Do I require WASA for any additional changes/module added to the Application?
items.answer: Yes, WASA is required for the add-on changes or add-on modules that are to be added in the application. Ensure that certificate for the said application is already issued and valid.

items.question: Is WASA required for entire application or specific module?
items.answer: The WASA is required for the entire application or specific module as per the requirement. The WASA for entire application is required if no WASA has been conducted for the application before moving to the production. The WASA is required separately for all modules if modules are being developed sequentially. For example, for an application 'XYZ' (in production for which WASA certificate has already been issued) an additional module A has been added. The WASA only needs to be conducted for the sequential module A subtracting the application part 'XYZ'.

items.question: Can integrator go ahead with WASA certification for common Base URL of ABHA functionality instead of separate WASA for IOS app, android App or website?
items.answer: WASA is required for all, i.e., WASA for IOS app, WASA for android app and for website also.

items.question: Is WASA required for Production URL or Staging URL?
items.answer: WASA is always required for hosting application in the production environment. It’s conducted on the Staging URL for which the certificate issued is licensed to the same application in the production.

items.question: Where should I get WASA done?
items.answer: Please refer: https://www.cert-in.org.in/PDF/Empanel_org_2021.pdf

items.question: Is the WASA required post any changes done in the module(s)/code?
items.answer: Yes, WASA is to be initiated again in case of any changes done in the module(s)/code. However, if the changes are minor, then the said can be ignored. However, if the changes are critical or major in nature and affects any changes in the backend etc., then WASA is mandatory.

items.question: What if I require one WASA for all the modules?
items.answer: If one WASA is required for multiple or all the modules, then the same needs to be developed for multiple or all the modules before applying for WASA certificate.
